questions.text: How does FlashAttention reduce the memory overhead of standard dense attention?

options.A: It discards all but the nearest key for each query.
options.B: It tiles computation and uses online softmax to avoid storing the full attention matrix in GPU main memory.
options.C: It removes softmax and replaces attention with an unweighted mean.
options.D: It caches generated text instead of computing query–key dot products.

questions.explanation: FlashAttention uses tiling and online softmax to compute dense attention without materializing the full N-by-N score/probability matrices in GPU main memory. It preserves the attention computation up to numerical differences.

questions.text: A KV cache has batch size 1, 2 layers, 4 KV heads, head dimension 8, and 10 cached tokens. At 2 bytes per element, how many bytes store the keys and values, excluding allocation overhead?
questions.explanation: K and V require 2 * layers * KV heads * head dimension * tokens * bytes = 2*2*4*8*10*2 = 2560 bytes.

questions.text:
After this code runs, what is len(cache.K[0][1])?

```python
class KVCache:
    def __init__(self, n_layers, n_heads):
        self.K = [[[] for _ in range(n_heads)] for _ in range(n_layers)]
        self.V = [[[] for _ in range(n_heads)] for _ in range(n_layers)]
    def append(self, layer, head, k, v):
        self.K[layer][head].append(k)
        self.V[layer][head].append(v)

cache = KVCache(1, 2)
cache.append(0, 1, [1, 2], [3, 4])
cache.append(0, 1, [5, 6], [7, 8])
```
questions.explanation: Each append adds one key vector to that head’s token list. Two appended vectors give a list length of two, regardless of vector width.
